body: **2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** — the MCP wait cap: §8 Timeout extensions says the MCP `wait` tool clamps `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms, which is also its default (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`). An MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` after 50 s, and CLI `viola wait` times out only on a timeout the caller passes. This is the origin of rows contract/mcp-wait-tool/timeout-ms and contract/viola-wait/timed-out. A wake-condition change to the MCP `wait` tool (`crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs`) must keep the cap and the timed-out answer, and the bound must stay on the driver only.

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — the dialog hold became configurable (`dialog_hold_s`, 60–3600, default 60). When the hold ends, the wrapper appends one `dialog-expired` line, and that line wakes `wait`. This is the origin of row contract/event-line/dialog-expired: `dialog-expired` is an existing wake kind that the documented wake/log-only split must keep. The hold bounds the driver and never the human.

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** — the first dialog deadline (60 s, later superseded by the configurable hold). It set the precedent that a time bound falls on the driver's path, with an expired dialog rendered for the human in the TUI. This chunk's turn-end question wake rests on that dialog/answer critical path (row decision/critical-path-dialog-answer).

**2026-11-15-live-round-on-the-trimmed-product** — `~ decision/dialog-hold-bounds-the-driver`: state changed from provisional to standing after the live measurement. The hold whose end appends the wake line `dialog-expired` is now ratified and is not this chunk's to re-open.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (the dialog hold bounds owned by 0.2.0's first entry) — `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` / `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX` stay PROVISIONAL, owned by 0.2.0's first entry. This applies if the wake-on-`dialog-expired` cases or the fake agent's turn scripts lean on the hold's bounds.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` and `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` dropped the budget pause from the list of time bounds. These are the closed lists of every bound viola holds (the wait timeout and cap among them). Any new or changed wait bound, or a re-arm, must be listed there and must fall on the driver.

**2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed** — `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` dropped the status-line deadline, which gives the rows their current wording (wait timeout and cap, dialog hold, readiness gate, confirm windows, agents read). Precedent: a chunk that adds or removes a time bound amends both twin rows.

**2026-10-10-session-links** — `wait` got a case of its own under a closed gate (`path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone`). This is precedent for driver-side `wait` readings that type no human key and read no terminal stream. The budget gate behind it was later removed (2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed).

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — §4 P6 records that `viola wait` and `viola --help` carry no ESC and no lone CR. This is the static-linear-output rule (rows decision/linear-static-cli-output, contract/viola-wait/waiting-line) that any change to `wait`'s human output (`src/human/wait.rs`) must keep.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (the cli SGR and escape checks; the a11y cases' CI home) — `viola wait`'s no-ESC/no-lone-CR check is now ungated on ubuntu-latest. The cli and tui cases run inside the `test` job's single `coverage` suite on the one `ubuntu-latest` leg, whose `gate --require coverage,doctest` is the verdict (row decision/a11y-cases-inside-coverage-suite). That job is where the carried `path1_run_start_one_home_in_order` TIMEOUT at the `ci` profile's 20 s kill was read.

**2026-10-16-remove-the-browser-leg** — the a11y cases became nextest cases in the `coverage` suite. The §10 failure condition became a `gate --require coverage,doctest` breach (`suite-failed`, `suite-skipped`, `suite-missing`, `artifact-missing`), and the zero-flakiness parallel bans `#[ignore]`. This is the origin of rows decision/a11y-gate-breach-fails-build and decision/zero-flakiness. The CI-red fix (a shared or copied stamped home, or a resized `ci` kill) may not skip, ignore or retry the timed-out case.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — CLI output-discipline evidence reports under CI's single instrumented `coverage` suite, gated by `gate --require coverage,doctest`. This is the base of rows decision/gate-requires-coverage-doctest and decision/ci-test-gate-no-skips, which bound how the `ci` profile and `tests/support/verify.rs` fix may change.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — `verify`'s interrupted pair: if `verify` is stopped before it finishes, it prints no step line and no summary. It prints only `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` and `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, then exits 1, and the stop path adds no time bound. This is the origin of row contract/viola-verify/interrupted-pair. It bears on the CI-red item: a stamped-home fixture whose `viola verify` is bounded or killed must not leave this pair's contract or the step-line row (contract/viola-verify/step-line).

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (a lost wrapper and a stale holder; exit 21's `--json` document names its cause) — a frame verb such as `wait` whose wrapper is lost with the call open reads `endpoint-lost`. Against a stale instance it reads `instance-dead`. Under `--json`, exit 21 gives one document whose `detail` is a closed cause word. A parked `wait` that ends on something other than a wake kind must keep these refusal shapes.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** (the `--json` failure documents' witness; `--json`'s one document and its exit-2 exception) — each `--json` failure is one document with a literal exit, empty stderr, no ESC byte and a clean body (`cli_error_documents_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text`). The one-document rule has an exception only for the `answer` and `send` exit-2 paths. These are the origins of rows contract/cli-json-failure/document, decision/json-failure-documents-are-clean, decision/json-one-document-no-hint and contract/cli-refusal/json, which `wait --json` stays inside.

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** (the plugin against an impostor wrapper writes no human-facing byte) — the first not-assertable entity for the plugin and MCP frame tools, `wait` among them. Precedent for row decision/no-assertions-for-plugin-and-ipc: the MCP `wait` tool's wake behaviour is proved by handler tests, not by a11y assertions.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** (the cli output-discipline checks on std::process::Command and literal pins; the §8 verification lines pinned by literal; the cli tooling in the a11y testing contracts) — trycmd and assert_cmd were replaced by literal pins over `std::process::Command`. Every fixed CLI string is pinned by a literal, so a copy change fails CI on purpose. This is the origin of rows decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned, decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned-by-literal, decision/cli-a11y-by-literal-tests and the c0-c1 / linear-output guards. Any new or changed `wait` string or waiting line takes a literal pin.

**2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list** — the row escape (ESC, C1, DEL, `\n`, `\t` → `\xHH`) for `viola list` rows. It is the basis of the list-row exception in rows decision/control-character-escaping and decision/control-bytes-escaped, while `wait` and `last` text keep `\n` and `\t` raw. Any text `wait` returns from a woken line must follow the wait/last rule and not the list-row one.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — the first live reading of the takeover clause, recorded as supplemental and never gating (row decision/live-readings-never-gate). Precedent for this chunk's boundary that a live `claude` start for the wake clause would be a supplemental reading, with the gating proof over the fake agent.

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** — the second live takeover reading on a real `claude` session, again supplemental and never gating. This confirms that live readings of the product never become CI gates, which bears on any wake-condition reading on claude 2.1.325.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — per-chunk and CI mutation gates were removed. Output-discipline invariants in crate tests meet mutation only at the epoch-boundary audit. This matches the chunk's «no mutation run» boundary, where each new guard is proved by a one-off remove-the-guard control instead.

**2026-11-12T03-23-49-rows** — the master became rows. Every picked row (time bounds, wait contracts, output discipline, CI gate) dates from this conversion, verified against the code at 8834195b0683. Amendments to them go by `+`/`~`/`−` on a row handle.

Documents and pins by tests the wake condition of `wait` (CLI `viola wait`, `wait --json`, MCP `wait`): which logged event kinds return a parked wait and which park it again, proved over the fake agent.
A turn end held by a background task wakes `wait` (the turn-ended line carrying background_tasks, or the question it raises); a task-free turn end's later log-only notification gives no false wake to a wait armed after that end.
Re-measures from the code and the fake agent whether a turn end reading 0 background tasks while the session still waits returns the wait and leaves the driver to re-arm, and re-reads today's wake kinds versus log-only kinds before stating them.
Takes the carried CI red as its own item: the stamped-home fixture's unbounded `viola verify` pushes the run-start test past the ci profile's 20 s kill; chosen by measurement between taking the stamping out of the measured time (a home stamped once and shared or copied) and sizing the class's ci kill to the loaded time.
No live claude start, no mutation run; each new guard test carries a one-off remove-the-guard control.

body: The `viola wait` human output: the waiting line naming the session while it parks, unchanged in wording by the new wake condition.
The `viola wait` timed_out result, human and --json, which a wait that is not woken still ends with.
The MCP wait tool and its timeout_ms value: the tool returns on the same wake kinds as the CLI verb.
The wait/last output as a critical path of the CLI: a wake on a background-task turn end or a question returns its result as static linear output.
Time bounds fall on the driver only, never on the human: the re-arm after a turn end with no background task is the driver's, and no wait timeout is put on the human at the terminal.
No harsh timeouts without warning: a wait's bound stays the caller-given timeout and ends in its timed-out result, never a silent drop.
The event line kinds the wait feed reads: the turn-ended line with background_tasks, the question, and the log-only notification kinds, as the event catalog names them.
--json output of `wait` stays one clean document with no hint line, on a wake as on a timeout.
Fixed CLI strings of `wait` stay pinned by their literals in the existing tests when the wake tests are added.
The `viola verify` step lines the stamped-home fixture produces: taking its run out of the measured time or bounding it changes no step line wording.
The CI test gate allows no skips and no retries: the run-start test's TIMEOUT is fixed by a bound shown to hold at load, never by skipping or retrying the test.
Live readings never gate: the wake condition is proved over the fake agent; any live claude reading is asked before and does not become a gating test.
Gate breach fails the build: the sized ci kill or the shared stamped home must keep the coverage suite's gate a hard fail.

each new test's failure is a nextest failure, run in the existing test suites
each new test is free of flakiness and passes with no retries
each new test runs inside the coverage suite in the GitHub Actions push/PR workflow

body: The TUI passthrough contracts and the boundary-driver rows (vendor content, viola terminal bytes, focus, mouse and resize sequences, human keystrokes, vt100 feed panic): the chunk changes no terminal passthrough.
The `viola list` board rows (caption order, colour, stale-row dim, NAME truncation, the unwrapped separator): the chunk prints no board.
The revive refusal and revive --list contracts: the chunk changes no revive path.
The link and unlink, plugin install and --help contracts: none of those verbs is touched.
The send refusals (input-not-ready, no-prompt-submitted) and send-refused-while-typing: send confirmation and the readiness-gate race are not this chunk's.
The frame-verb, hook-call and MCP frame-tool refusals for server-verify, socket directory and strict modes: the chunk adds no frame or hook refusal.
The manual Orca and keyboard passes and the screen-reader targets: supplemental, gate nothing, and the chunk adds no manual pass.
The absences (web or graphical frontend, touch surface, internationalization) and the WCAG mapping and contrast harness areas: nothing in them applies to a wait wake condition.

**2026-10-04-wait-and-last** (wait and last as built) — set `wait` to `{after?, timeout_ms?, from?}`, its start offset at `after` or else at the log's end, and the line-starts rule. It added `EventKind::WAIT_WAKE` and the `WaitFeed` wake: one Mutex + Condvar, the hook line appended inside the lock, only hook lines signal, and 20 ms clock re-reads that never re-scan. An `after`-less wait starts at the log end. Why it matters: this is the mechanism this chunk documents and pins. A turn end followed by a notification is decided here, by which kinds are in `WAIT_WAKE` and by the fact that a no-cursor wait sees only later lines.

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** (hook.dialog, answer, the deadline) — made a pending dialog come first in `wait`: an `after`-less wait, or one at or before the dialog's line, returns it at once, through `WaitFeed::appending_dialog` / `dialog_settled`. Why it matters: the turn-end question this chunk must wake on rides this pending-dialog path (contract/channel-wait/pending-dialog, contract/channel-methods/wait-pending-dialog).

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** (the configurable dialog hold and the dialog-expired record) — added `dialog-expired` as the one wrapper-appended kind that wakes `wait`, which made the wake set six (`turn-ended` · `question` · `permission` · `plan` · `session-end` · `dialog-expired`), with "only hook lines signal" now excepting it. It also moved the `pending_dialog` write ahead of the event line. Why it matters: this is the wake set the chunk restates and pins, and the one precedent for a wrapper line that wakes.

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** (`question` gains `option_details`, `turn-ended` gains `background_tasks`) — made `turn-ended` data `{last_assistant_message, background_tasks}`. `background_tasks` is a count only of the Stop payload's array, or `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array. The founder answered the count-only form himself. Why it matters: the chunk's case of "a turn end held by a background task" is read through this field. Any wake rule keyed on it is bounded by the count-only, no-element-read form.

**2026-11-15-api-error-turn-end** (Standard Contracts: 3 rows) — gave `turn-ended` data an optional `cause` (`api-error` only, PROVISIONAL), so it is now `{last_assistant_message, background_tasks, cause?}`. It added decision/api-error-turn-end-clears-turn. Why it matters: a StopFailure turn end is a second source of `turn-ended` that wakes `wait`. The pinned wake cases must cover it, and they must not move the provisional `cause` contract, whose founder ratification is still owed.

**2026-11-15-api-error-turn-end** (Conventions: 2 rows; Established Decisions: 3 rows; Cross-cutting Patterns: 1 row; Design Philosophy: 1 row) — added contract/hook-to-kind-map/stopfailure (StopFailure → `turn-ended`) and contract/turn-end-cause/cause-set. It put StopFailure in the sync spine tiers and registered the StopFailure exception ("provisionally, no ledger row and no verify probe") on decision/capability-ledger, decision/cli-capability-ledger and decision/capability-ledger-gate. Why it matters: the hook-to-kind map is where this chunk states which hooks wake. The StopFailure live reading and its ledger exception are out of scope for this chunk, so the plan must leave them as they stand.

**2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events** (seven exec-form hooks, `hook.event` served) — registered Notification, PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure as `async: true` hooks, and set `hook.event`'s five hook kinds with `activity` among them. Why it matters: a notification reaches the log as `activity`, which is log-only (contract/hook-to-kind-map/notification, contract/hook-tiers/async). That kind is the "no false wake" line this chunk must pin.

**2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records** (confirmed send: kinds, refusals, exits) — added the wrapper-appended, log-only kinds `send-issued` · `send-confirmed` · `send-refused`. Why it matters: these are among the kinds the chunk's test must show re-park a wait (decision/wrapper-events-log-only, contract/channel-wait/wake-kinds).

**2026-10-10-session-links** (the implicit link as landed, the explicit verbs held) — added `link` to the wrapper-appended kinds, log-only, and to the `wait` row's list of wrapper lines that never wake. Why it matters: it is a precedent for how each new log-only kind was added to the never-wake list. A further log-only kind follows the same pattern.

**2026-10-26-explicit-session-links** (a product path appends the unlink event) — made a product path append `unlink` and added it to the `wait` records that never wake (the `send-*`, `link`, `unlink` and start records). Why it matters: this is the current never-wake list the chunk's documentation restates (contract/channel-wait/wake-kinds).

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** (Standard Contracts: wrapper-events-log-only, both rows; Conventions: budget-gate kind removed) — removed `budget-gate` from the wrapper-appended log-only kinds and from the normalised event kinds. Every own-format `v` stayed at 1. Why it matters: the log-only list the chunk pins no longer holds `budget-gate`. An older log's `budget-gate` line is now an unknown kind that the reader skips, and it must not wake.

**2026-11-15-live-round-on-the-trimmed-product** (Established Decisions: 4 rows) — moved the dialog hold and its bound to standing. It also said that at the hold's end the expiry ends only the hook's wait while the CLI's dialog stays drawn (contract/dialog-hold-end/null-reply). Why it matters: a woken `wait` on `dialog-expired` does not mean the dialog is gone. This is relevant to how the chunk documents what each wake means.

**2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host** (the paste hint measured on the live CLI) — measured that a no-cursor `viola wait` issued in the hint window woke on nothing and ran to its deadline, while `wait --after` the earlier cursor returned at once. Why it matters: this is a measured precedent for the no-cursor vs cursor behaviour. The overseer's waiter re-arm (the scope's `[inferred]` item) turns on the same start-offset rule (contract/channel-wait/after, contract/channel-wait/start-offset).

**2026-10-04-running-turn-refusal** (the running-turn state as built) — keyed the running-turn state on kind alone: `prompt-submitted` starts it, `turn-ended` / `session-start` / `session-end` end it, and `activity` leaves it. Why it matters: it is the existing kind-keyed rule beside `WAIT_WAKE` that treats `activity` as inert. A wake rule that tells a held turn end apart must not contradict it.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** (the MCP tools' contract as landed) — made MCP `wait` send `timeout_ms` = `min(given, 50 000)` (`WAIT_CAP`), 50 000 ms by default, with `after` passed as given. Each handler re-validates its raw arguments. Why it matters: the MCP `wait` surface the chunk pins carries this cap (decision/mcp-wait-cap). A parked MCP wait returns `{timed_out:true}` at 50 s regardless of wake kinds.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** (the Tokio client and viola-channel's tree-form ban) — put MCP `wait` on `viola-channel`'s feature-gated `TokioClient`, while CLI `wait` stays a blocking read on the sync client. Why it matters: the chunk's `crates/viola-mcp/src/tools.rs` surface and decision/tokio-containment / decision/hybrid-concurrency bound where any wait change may live.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (the exit-21 document carries its cause in `detail`) — made a `wait` whose endpoint vanishes read `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `endpoint-lost` (contract/channel-wait/timeout-ms). Why it matters: a blocked wait that ends with no event is part of the wake contract the chunk documents.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (a client's refused socket directory; the peer euid on both sides) — fixed the frame-writing clients' order: the strict-modes check, the liveness pre-check, `check_endpoint_dir`, the peer euid, then the server identity check. CLI `wait` and MCP `wait` both run it. Why it matters: decision/frame-client-check-order binds any change to `src/cmd/wait.rs` or the MCP `wait` tool. No check may be reordered.

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** (the snapshot's pid and started_at as the server identity) — made the `wait` client, CLI and MCP, compare the peer pid and OS start time with the snapshot's before its first frame. Why it matters: these are the rows decision/verify-server-before-first-frame and decision/server-identity-check-before-frame. Tests that drive `wait` go through this check.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (the instance check first at every CLI frame verb and MCP frame tool) — made `wait` (CLI through `client::refuse_untrusted`, MCP in `frame`) run `check_instance` before any snapshot read. A refusal is exit 21 with no line. Why it matters: decision/instance-check-before-any-read, decision/client-strict-modes-before-frame and decision/mcp-frame-tools-strict-modes-check all bind the wait surfaces this chunk touches.

**2026-10-10-self-healing-state** (the next append heals a torn last line; the reader counts three names) — made the next append heal a torn last line. `events::read_from` counts `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`, and does not return an unknown kind. Why it matters: the wait feed reads `events.ndjson`. An unknown or torn line must neither wake nor move a cursor wrongly (decision/append-heals-torn-line, decision/reader-counts-skipped-lines, decision/events-log-never-truncated).

**2026-10-10-session-links** (the link set in the replay, the snapshot and the start) — fixed that a start reads `events.ndjson` twice before the endpoint serves (`WaitFeed::rebuild`, then `LinkSet::restore`). Why it matters: `WaitFeed::rebuild` is the start-time step that seeds `last` (contract/channel-last/last-assistant-message) and the feed. A change to the feed's state must keep that rebuild order.

**2026-10-05-permission-end-to-end** (the question first raised by PermissionRequest stays null) — logged a `question` first raised by PermissionRequest once and answered it `null` at once. A later answer is `unknown-dialog`. Why it matters: such a question still appends a `question` line that wakes `wait` (decision/permission-request-question-stays-null). That is a wake case beside the turn-end question.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** (the fake agent's agents mode) — added the `agents` mode word and files beside the fake agent's executable. This was the founder's own answer that there be no third fake-agent env seam. Why it matters: the chunk extends the fake agent's turn scripts (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `fixtures/fake-scripts/`). A new knob takes the argv, script or mode-word route, never a new env seam (decision/fake-agent-test-seams).

**2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate** (the second fake-agent test seam `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC`) — ratified a second fake-agent env seam as a boundary widening. The founder ruled it live. Why it matters: it is a precedent that any further fake-agent env seam is a widening needing the founder's word (decision/fake-agent-test-seams, decision/viola-env-namespace-product-only).

**2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows** (the 2.1.302 fixture set and the long-turn screen switch) — counted the fake agent's argv options at thirteen (the count's rule is architecture's own list) and added `--long-turn-screen`. Why it matters: a turn-script option added for a background-task or notification case moves this registered count. The count must be updated by its rule.

**2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness** (verify's spawn pairs, the harness CI read, verify-stamped homes) — made root rstest homes stamped by `stamped_home` through `viola verify` against the fake agent. Why it matters: this is the fixture behind the carried CI red. `path1_run_start_one_home_in_order`'s extra time sits in the unbounded `viola verify` at `tests/support/verify.rs`. Option (a), stamping once and sharing, changes this design.

**2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows** (the resume row, Run E and /compact listed) — made verify drive five interactive runs, so a verify is six `claude` starts. Why it matters: it explains why the `stamped_home` fixture's verify costs ~5 s even under the fake agent. That cost grows with load, and it is the time the chunk must take out of the measured window or size the `ci` kill to.

**2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume** (the test homes' base, its keepers and the dev host's tmpfs backing) — made the dev host's `target/e2e-home` a tmpfs link. It also set the standing rule that "a stalled-start red is a finding about the backing, reported and never re-run for green". Why it matters: this is the rule for the carried `path1_run_start_one_home_in_order` timeout. The chunk's measured choice between (a) and (b) must not re-run for green, and any shared stamped home lives under these keepers.

**2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup** (the keepers' headroom floor and the census's second form) — added the `HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB` (9 GiB) refusal after the stamped-home gates hit EDQUOT on the dev host's tmpfs. Why it matters: stamped homes are a measured disk and time cost. Sharing or copying one stamped home (option a) interacts with this floor and with the keepers' isolation.

**2026-10-02-epoch-2b-cleanup** (test homes removed with their owner record last) — routed both removals of a test home through `remove_owned`, which deletes `owner.json` last. Why it matters: a home stamped once and shared or copied across tests must keep the owner-record sweep rule (decision/test-home-owner-sweep, decision/test-homes-cleaned-by-owner).

**2026-11-15-mutation-and-coverage-baselines-green** (Occupied Resources: 2 rows) — raised the shared root `WITHIN` bound from 7 s to 12 s (decision/root-waits-share-one-bound) and moved test channel sockets under a short `/tmp` root. Why it matters: the chunk's new wait tests share this one bound. Sizing the `ci` kill or a wait is the same kind of change, made the chunk before.

**2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup-ii** (the Watch bound's waits counted by pattern) — made the count's rule the `Instant::now() + WITHIN` pattern rather than a census. body: The wait contract's wake kinds: which logged kinds return a parked wait and which (activity, wheel and other log-only records) park it again, stated and pinned for the channel wait method, `viola wait` and the MCP `wait` tool.

A turn ending while a background task still holds the session wakes the wait: the wait returns on the `turn-ended` line carrying `background_tasks`, or on the `question` the turn end raises, and never parks past it.

No false wake: after a turn ended with no background task, a later notification-class line that is log-only does not return a fresh wait armed after that end; the wait instead runs to its timeout or the next real wake.

The `turn-ended` event data and its `background_tasks` key (and the Stop event data's null details), as the wake decision reads them; whether a 0 count while the session still waits on a notification is documented behaviour, a defect, or the driver's to re-arm is settled at P3 from the code before the plan states it.
The wait's cursor: a wait armed after a turn end does not return on a line already past its after cursor, and a line already logged past the cursor returns at once.
The wait timeout and the MCP wait bound (`timeout_ms`): a non-waking case is observed as a `timed_out` result inside the bound, never by a sleep.
CLI and MCP return identical payloads: the wake and the timed-out result read the same through `viola wait --json` and the MCP `wait` tool.

Proof over the fake agent: new turn-script steps (a background task held at turn end, a notification line after a task-free end) follow the fake agent turn-script format and gated steps, configured by argv alone, and the fake agent stays held to the recorded fixtures.
Test waits key on logged events: the wake tests synchronise on event lines and the event log, with no sleep and no retry; wait wake latency is not timed.

The carried CI red is this chunk's item: `path1_run_start_one_home_in_order` timing out at the `ci` profile's 20 s kill (run ci#43773402286, sha 7fd86141, job `test (ubuntu-latest)`), the extra time sitting in the stamped-home fixture's unbounded `viola verify`; acceptance is a bound the plan can show holding at load.

Option (a) for the CI red: take the stamping out of the stamped-home tests' measured time — a home stamped once and shared or copied — naming the per-test-home isolation it costs, with stamps still written only by `viola verify` against the fake agent and no product state hand-written.

Option (b) for the CI red: size the stamped-home class's `ci` kill to the fixture's loaded time, staying coherent with the 20 s kill line for stamped-home and verify-driven tests, the mutants kill lines below cargo-mutants' timeout, and root waits bounded below the kills.
The CI test profile keeps no retries and the zero-flakiness budget: the CI red is fixed by a bound, never by a retry or a skipped or ignored test.
Each new guard test carries its one-off remove-the-guard control through `gate.py control`, the control's case being the test's name alone; no mutation run is made in this chunk.

No live `claude` start without asking first: the plan runs on the fake agent; a fake-agent run is not proof of real-CLI behaviour, so a wake clause that needs a live reading on claude 2.1.325 is named with its start count and asked before the card, and any granted start runs under a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, never in CI.
Unknown or forward-compatible event lines met by the wait feed are counted and skipped, never a wake and never a failure.
The `viola wait` failure exits stay as they are around the change: endpoint-lost and an unreachable or killed wrapper still end a parked wait with their own cause.
